native_result.query: In which century do Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form show opposite growth trends for the first time, with Pottery Decoration increasing significantly and Pottery Form declining simultaneously?
native_result.HypoA: In 1700 BCE, for the first time, Diversity in Pottery Decoration shows a significant increase while Diversity in Pottery Form experiences a notable decline. This marks a unique divergence in the growth trends of these two cultural capital variables.
native_result.HypoB: Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form first show opposite growth trends in the 18th century BCE, around 1700 BCE: Pottery Decoration diversity rises sharply (z-score -0.48 to +0.97, delta = +1.45, about 3.4 SD of its historical century-to-century variability) while Pottery Form diversity drops simultaneously to its lowest recorded level (+0.74 to -1.13, delta = -1.87). This is the only century in the entire 4300-500 BCE record where Decoration increases and Form declines simultaneously, coinciding with the Late Neolithic-to-Bronze-Age (LN to OBA) cultural transition. Archaeologically, this marks a reorganization of ceramic production: vessel forms became standardized (form diversity collapsing to a plateau of -1.13 lasting to 500 BCE) while decorative diversity was elaborated to its maximum (+0.97 to +1.53), i.e., a divergent style strategy in which standardized shapes were differentiated through surface ornamentation.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data/time_series_data.csv (3601 annual rows, CE -4100..-500). Extracted the 37 century bins where raw PotteryDecoration/PotteryForm z-scores are observed; verified _inter series are exact linear interpolations (max residual 2.2e-16) and identical to raw on the century grid. Computed century-to-century changes dDec and dForm; scanned chronologically from 4300 BCE for the first bin with dDec >= +0.5 z-units AND dForm < 0 (sensitivity: dDec >= 1 SD of changes = 0.431; loosest: any Decoration rise). Triangulated with a 100-year rolling smoothed derivative of the annual _inter series (opposite-trend window CE -1800..-1601, centered on the 1700 BCE bin). Cross-validated all 37 century values against capital.csv (exact match, max |diff| = 0), including cultural period labels (LN to OBA transition). Thresholds are deterministic decision rules, not statistical tests (z-scores without an error model).
